articles.title: “I think he is a role model for young people”: How LeBron James’ $2 million gift transformed “The Decision” into a life-changing moment for kids
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James’ “The Decision” became infamous on July 8, 2010, when he announced his move from the Cleveland Cavaliers to the Miami Heat during a live .
articles.body: LeBron James’ “The Decision” became infamous on July 8, 2010, when he announced his move from the Cleveland Cavaliers to the Miami Heat during a live ESPN special. But behind the controversial announcement was a charity plan that raised more than $2.5 million for Boys & Girls Clubs across the country. The money helped support youth programs and improve facilities, turning a heavily criticized night into something that gave children a lasting benefit.James chose the Boys & Girls Club of Greenwich, Connecticut, as the setting for the broadcast. The club hosted the event as millions watched James reveal his next team. Yet the most important part of the night had little to do with Miami. LeBron James used “The Decision” to put millions toward children and their communitiesThe charity plan came together just days before the broadcast. On July 7, 2010, ESPN confirmed that proceeds from “The Decision” would go to Boys & Girls Clubs of America to support James’ vision of building basketball courts for young people across the country. James and his marketing company, LRMR Marketing, secured sponsors for the event.The final impact went beyond the initial expectations. Boys & Girls Clubs of America reported that the special generated more than $2.5 million for Clubs in seven markets: Akron, Chicago, Cleveland, Greenwich, Los Angeles, Miami and New York. The money supported youth programs, facility improvements and refurbishment projects.LeBron James later explained why he wanted the announcement to benefit the organization. During his July 9, 2010 appearance on “Good Morning America,” James said, “All the proceeds from the announcement was going to the Boys and Girls Club.” He added that he was happy to be in a position to help because “when you do something for them and you do something that's positive, they never forget about it.”There was another important detail. LeBron James did not make money from the broadcast. Frank Sanchez of Boys & Girls Clubs of America told the Christian Science Monitor on July 9, 2010, that James’ intention was to use the enormous attention around his free agency “to raise dollars and awareness” for the organization. Sanchez added, “LeBron didn’t make a penny” from the event.The Greenwich kids saw a different side of LeBron James that nightThe Boys & Girls Club of Greenwich received about $90,000 from the proceeds, along with 15 desktop computers and several laptops. The money helped refurbish the gym floor and add padding around the court, giving the children a better place to play.The night also created personal memories for the young members inside the club. After the broadcast, James interacted with the children and helped make the event feel less like a television production.That experience stayed with Bob DeAngelo, the club’s executive director at the time. He initially admitted that he was not a James fan. Ten years later, his view had changed significantly.Speaking to The Athletic for its July 8, 2020 retrospective on “The Decision,” DeAngelo said, “I think he means well and I think he is a role model for young people.” He also explained how James’ actions after that night changed his opinion: “That got erased as he went on his journey.”That journey included championships, community work and a much larger public platform. But the charitable side of July 8, 2010, remains one of the clearest reminders that “The Decision” was more than a free-agency announcement.James changed teams that night. He also helped change what a Boys & Girls Club could provide for the children who depended on it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "These kids deserve better": Stephen Curry's wife Ayesha Curry opens up about the painful moment that changed their mission in Oakland
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have been actively trying to provide a better life to countless children living in their hometown, Oakland, .
articles.body: Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have been actively trying to provide a better life to countless children living in their hometown, Oakland, through their foundation, Eat. Learn & Play. While both of them have remained committed to it, Ayesha Curry has opened up about the moment they realised they need to do more.Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry reflects on the moment they realised they should do more for the children in oaklandIn an interview with the Hollywood Reporter, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry said, “At one of our first playground builds, final touches were being done and the kids were brought out for a little ceremony to celebrate the opening of the playground, the outdoor learning center and the gardens.”The popular actress added, “The kids were celebrating, but one little girl came out a little hysterical. As she was being consoled, everyone was wondering what was wrong. She asked, “Where are we going to school now?” It took a minute to realize that she asked because she thought other kids were going to come in and use that space.”Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry continued, “She didn’t think that she was deserving of a new space. That, for me, was a very foundational moment of realizing that these kids deserve better. They shouldn’t feel like it’s a present. This should be the expectation and the standard of what they deserve. It was a huge eye-opening moment.”Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry continue to change lives across their hometownOver the last seven years, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have invested their own funds and have been able to raise millions through donations as they have sought to provide a better life to children belonging to underprivileged families in Oakland.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat. Learn & Play was set up to provide meals and education to children but for the last seven years, it has done more than that.Through their foundation, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have also made sure more and more children take sports seriously and have been able to increase participation in middle school sports by 300%.Both of them have remained closely associated with the people from their hometown, Oakland, as they constantly look for new ways to be there for the children belonging to underprivileged backgrounds.While Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s efforts have been commendable, they have often been asked about not branching out to other states and doing the same.The two have not really confirmed the reason but they have hinted that they might be looking to extend their services in other states as well.For now, they remain committed to their hometown as they try to manage their busy lifestyles.With weeks left for the new season to begin, Stephen Curry puts his focus on his career as he recovers from brutal injuries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Angel Reese Ruling on 8th Technical Foul Made By WNBA, Will Dream Star Be Suspended?
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese has avoided a one-game suspension after the WNBA rescinded her latest technical foul, according to Doug Feinberg of the Associated Press.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese has avoided a one-game suspension after the WNBA rescinded her latest technical foul, according to Doug Feinberg of the Associated Press.

Reese was assessed her eighth tech of the season in the fourth quarter of the Dream's Friday night loss to the visiting Portland Fire.

She appeared to make contact with the Fire's Carla Leite before picking up the foul.

WNBA regulations require players who have received seven technical fouls pay a $1,500 fine and serve a one-game suspension for each additional tech.

Reese had earlier in the game tied Alyssa Thomas for the WNBA's single-season record for double-doubles with her 28th of the season.

She finished out the contest having shot 5-for-14 with 16 points and 16 rebounds.

Reese reached the technical foul limit last season while playing for the Chicago Sky.

She served out that suspension in the fourth-to-last game of a season in which the Sky had already been eliminated from playoff contention.

The Dream are in a notably different position after clinching a playoff spot last Saturday following a win over the Phoenix Mercury in which Reese scored a career-high 31 points.

Atlanta is now in a tight race with multiple clubs including the Las Vegas Aces and Indiana Fever for better playoff seeding.

The Dream already took a step back in that race after conceding a Friday loss to the Fire while the Fever won their own matchup the same night against the Connecticut Sun.

Luckily for the Dream, they'll have their top rebounder available for Sunday's matchup against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx after her technical foul was rescinded.

The Dream will take on the No. 1 seed at 3 p.m. ET on Sunday in College Park.

articles.title: Denver Nuggets bid farewell to 6-foot-9 brother of WNBA star following Peyton Watson sign-and-trade
articles.summary: NBA News: The Denver Nuggets moved fast once the paperwork cleared. A little over a week after landing Julian Reese as a throw-in from Washington in the Peyton .
articles.body: The Denver Nuggets moved fast once the paperwork cleared. A little over a week after landing Julian Reese as a throw-in from Washington in the Peyton Watson sign-and-trade, Denver formally waived the 6-foot-9 forward/center on Friday, according to NBA.com's transaction log. The corner of the deal barely got the ink dry before it unwound.Reese arrived in the deal because he fit a specific structural gap: Denver sits above the league's second tax apron, and two-way contracts don't count against the cap. That made him cheap enough to absorb even for a team with no roster spot to spare. It also meant his stay was never guaranteed. For Reese, who is the brother of WNBA star Angel Reese and spent last season fighting for NBA minutes on a two-way deal in Washington, the waiver is one more stop in a path that has run through an undrafted draft class, a Summer League tryout and three organizations in under a year.CategoryDetailPlayerJulian ReesePosition/heightForward/center, 6-foot-9Current teamDenver Nuggets (waived Aug. 28, 2026)Previous teamWashington WizardsContract statusTwo-way contract, acquired via Peyton Watson sign-and-trade (Aug. 20, 2026)Nuggets waive Julian ReeseDenver's decision became official Friday when the team waived Reese, confirmed through NBA.com's transaction log. The corresponding open roster spot leaves KJ Simpson and 2026 second-round pick Bryce Hopkins as the only two-way players left on Denver's roster. Reese now has to clear waivers before he can sign elsewhere, a step that puts his next NBA opportunity in the hands of 29 other front offices before he's a true free agent again.Nuggets acquire Peyton WatsonReese only became a Nugget because Denver needed a mechanism, not a player. The Nuggets sit above the NBA's second tax apron, a status that blocks most roster additions. Two-way contracts, though, don't count against the cap, which let Denver absorb Reese's deal on Aug. 20 as part of the broader package that sent Peyton Watson to Washington in a sign-and-trade. The structural fit, not Reese's on-court role, decided his one-week tenure in Denver.Reese's brief run with the WizardsBefore the trade, Reese had shown flashes in Washington. Filling in at center for an injury-depleted frontcourt, he posted 18 points and 20 rebounds (10 offensive, 10 defensive) against Utah on March 5, the first Wizards player to do that since Antawn Jamison in 2010. He followed with 26 points and 17 rebounds against the Jazz on March 25. Across 13 games, the 23-year-old averaged 11.8 points, 10.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 30.9 minutes, plus 8.7 points and 7.4 rebounds over 41 G League appearances with Toronto's affiliate.Reese's ledger from the past year runs through transactions more than highlight reels: an undrafted class out of Maryland, a Summer League stint with the Lakers, an Exhibit 10 deal with Toronto in October, a two-way contract with Washington in February, and now a waiver from a team that held his rights for nine days. Clearing waivers, not his numbers, decides where he lands next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: NBA News: Sophie Cunningham has added another major partnership during a breakout year with the Indiana Fever. On Aug. 17, 2026, Once Upon A Coconut announced t.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has added another major partnership during a breakout year with the Indiana Fever. On Aug. 17, 2026, Once Upon A Coconut announced the WNBA guard as its newest brand ambassador. The deal stands out because the company donates 10% of its profits to charity, giving Cunningham a chance to connect her growing platform with a cause she already values.The partnership comes as Cunningham continues to build her profile both on and off the court. With millions of social media followers and several major brands behind her, this latest deal gives her another way to reach fans while supporting a community-focused message.Sophie Cunningham’s latest Once Upon A Coconut partnership puts giving back in focusOnce Upon A Coconut announced the partnership with Cunningham on Aug. 17, 2026. The agreement will put the Fever guard in national advertisements, social media campaigns, retail promotions and community initiatives as the beverage company continues expanding its reach.The company says it built its brand around natural coconut water and a mission that goes beyond selling drinks. Once Upon A Coconut donates 10% of its profits to charitable causes, making that commitment a major part of its identity.Cunningham addressed the partnership in the company’s announcement on August 17. She said, “I’m proud to represent a brand so committed to giving back to the community.”That line explains why the partnership carries more weight than a typical endorsement. Cunningham has plenty of brands to choose from, including Adidas, European Wax Center, Arby’s, Marriott Bonvoy and Quest Nutrition. This deal gives her another opportunity to attach her name to something that supports charitable work.Once Upon A Coconut founder and CEO John Chiorando also explained the decision to work with Cunningham. In the August 17 announcement, he praised her toughness and resilience while pointing to her compassion and camaraderie with teammates.The company plans to bring Cunningham into its broader marketing push as it expands into more retail locations and other consumer spaces. So, the partnership gives both sides something beyond a standard advertising campaign. Cunningham gets another national platform, while the brand gains a recognizable WNBA personality who already has a strong connection with fans.Sophie Cunningham’s $10,182 fundraiser showed her community sideThat charitable connection also has a history. In 2025, Cunningham became the focus of a fan-led fundraiser connected to WNBA fines. What started as a joke eventually raised more than $10,000. Cunningham then chose to donate the money to Ronald McDonald House Charities instead of using it for herself.The fundraiser raised $10,182 from 171 donations, according to reports. Cunningham had also supported Ronald McDonald House Charities before, dating back to 2015.That decision showed how Cunningham could turn an unusual situation into something useful for other people. Her connection with the organization also predates her current Fever spotlight.Her community work has continued through basketball. Cunningham has hosted youth basketball events and camps, giving young players opportunities to learn from a professional WNBA athlete.That makes her latest partnership feel like a natural extension of what Cunningham has already done. Her profile is growing, but so is the reach of the causes she can support.Now, Once Upon A Coconut gives her another platform to do exactly that. The 10% profit donation comes from the company, but Cunningham’s role adds a personal connection to a message she has supported away from the court.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NBA forward Jonathan Kuminga's agent, Aaron Turner, revealed in an interview on Run It Back why his client signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves.
articles.body:
NBA forward Jonathan Kuminga's agent, Aaron Turner, revealed in an interview on Run It Back why his client signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Kuminga, who turns 24 on Oct. 6, has played five NBA seasons: a four-plus-year campaign with the Golden State Warriors and a couple of months with the Atlanta Hawks after the Dubs traded him there last February. He averaged 12.2 points on 46.3 percent shooting, 5.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 23.1 minutes per game last season.

Lakers' Top Targets After Kuminga Miss 🎯

Kuminga has a great opportunity with the Timberwolves, who should be a solid Western Conference contender once again. Minnesota made the Western Conference Finals in 2024 and 2025 and the second round in 2026 and could be in line for another playoff run yet again after trading for Charlotte Hornets point guard LaMelo Ball.

This could also be a one-and-done situation. Kuminga signed a two-year, $12.4 million contract with a player option for 2027-28, so he could be entering free agency again next offseason.

Kuminga had a much more lucrative deal on the table via the Warriors, but it appears his camp has eyes on next offseason in hopes of a better free agency haul.

On the bright side, this play may work out. Kuminga, who could very well start at forward, may break out in Minnesota, enjoy great success and set himself up for a lucrative deal.

However, Kuminga's former teammate, Draymond Green, pointed out a potential pitfall as well.

Former NBA guard Gilbert Arenas also wasn't seeing it.

The Timberwolves were already one of the league's most fascinating teams to watch next season after adding Ball. Still, now that's the case even more so after adding Kuminga, whose gamble on himself will be one to watch moving forward. He absolutely has the potential to win this one, but it's a risk nevertheless.

articles.title: Angel Reese ties Alyssa Thomas for most double-doubles in WNBA season, avoids suspension after 8th technical foul is rescinded
articles.summary: Earlier this week, Reese, a three-time All-Star, set the W's single-game and single-season rebounding records with a 26-board performance.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese rebounded from a scoreless first quarter Friday night against the Portland Fire to notch her 28th double-double of the 2026 campaign, tying Phoenix Mercury frontcourt standout Alyssa Thomas for the most in single-season WNBA history.

However, Reese shot only 5 of 14 in a 101-83 defeat and picked up her eighth technical foul of the season. That would have triggered an automatic one-game suspension, but the league was quickly reported to have rescinded the tech.

Reese, who finished with 16 points and 16 boards, was T'd up in the fourth quarter after she and Fire guard Carla Leite got tangled up in the lane.

A player or coach receiving their eighth technical foul during a WNBA regular-season results in a one-game suspension, per league rules. Every technical beyond that threshold comes with a $1,500 fine. And every two additional regular-season technicals following the eighth carry another one-game suspension.

Last season with the Chicago Sky, Reese served a one-game suspension once she was administered her eighth technical . She would have been set to miss Sunday's home game against the Minnesota Lynx this time around.

While the technical, poor shooting and game outcome poured some cold water on her recent hot streak, Reese still made some more history Friday night.

Four days earlier, she set the W's single-game and single-season rebounding records in Los Angeles with a 26-board performance during a victory over the Sparks . And now she shares the single-season double-double title with Thomas.

Thomas, a six-time All-Star, logged her 28 double-doubles in 2023 with the Connecticut Sun. Along the way, she piled up double-digit points and assists 11 times. Six of those outings featured triple-doubles (no other WNBA player has more than five triple-doubles all-time, and Thomas has 22 and counting for her career ).

All of Reese's double-doubles this season have resulted from her scoring 10-plus points and mounting 10-plus rebounds, the first of which came in her Dream regular-season debut . It's worth noting, however, that she's stacked at least five assists in five of her double-doubles. On Friday, she added six helpers to her stat line.

Notably, she sniffed a triple-double last week in a road win over the Sparks that saw her amass 20 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists. That night, she shot 9 of 9 from the field, including 2 of 2 from beyond the arc, and her Dream rewrote a single-game franchise record with 124 points .

Reese scored a career-high 31 points this past Saturday while helping Atlanta take down Thomas' Mercury on the road . The Dream clinched a playoff berth in the process.

The 24-year-old three-time All-Star has elevated her game in her first season with the Dream, who acquired the LSU product in a trade with the Sky this spring . She's averaging north of 16 points per game, and she entered Friday with a league-leading 12.4 rebounds per game.

articles.title: Kentucky Wildcats News: UK vs. the NCAA
articles.summary: Will UK be able to key players eligible for next season?
articles.body:
The Alex Afari and Mark Mitchell saga continues as they continue to fight for their eligibility.

The controversy stems from the NCAA's new eligibility structure, which does not grant athletes from the 2022 high school class who exhausted their eligibility in 2025-26 another season.

Mitchell took the issue to court and received a temporary injunction on August 21, allowing him to enter the transfer portal before committing to Kentucky.

However, another hurdle emerged when the SEC reaffirmed its rule prohibiting intraconference transfers who did not enter the portal during the spring window.

Mitchell's attorneys have since amended their complaint as the battle with the NCAA and SEC continues.

Afari briefly rejoined Kentucky after a federal ruling granted 2022 athletes another season, but an appeals court stayed that decision. He is now attempting to join Mitchell's Kentucky lawsuit.

The NCAA filed its opposition Friday, and Afari's next major step comes Monday when his case returns to court.

These are two game-changers for both programs, so it'll be interesting if they can both suit up.

The girls are starting the season exactly where they left off!

articles.title: ‘So coachable’ – Stephanie White says she’s ‘so proud’ of Indiana Fever player
articles.summary: Stephanie White has recently praised Indiana Fever player Makayla Timpson following her development in the 2026 season. Timpson was selected in the second ro...
articles.body:
Stephanie White has recently praised Indiana Fever player Makayla Timpson following her development in the 2026 season.

Timpson was selected in the second round of the 2025 WNBA draft by the Fever and made her debut for her new team on May 17 of that year.

She was then used sparingly in the remainder of last season, but her role has continued to grow in 2026, and White has now expressed how proud she is of Makayla.

Stephanie White proud of Makayla Timpson

Timpson made her first career start on July 17, 2026, and most recently played for the Fever in their win over the Connecticut Sun on Friday.

Makayla featured for 29 minutes, scoring 10 points and providing one assist as her team secured a 111-91 win over the Sun.

Now, White has been asked about the 23-year-old's development in her post-game media interview and expressed that she is 'so proud' of her.

The Fever coach also added that Timpson is 'so coachable' and a great template for young players.

White said: "I mean, look, I know I always say this, but I'm so proud of her. You know, it's as a rookie, you come in and your head's just spinning often times, and then you go into a first offseason and you have no idea what to expect, what to do, because in college, they hold your hand all the time.

"And when we had some hard conversations with KK in February and she came in and she got to work. So the results and the reward is because she was willing to do the work. And so I'm proud of her for that. You know, Keith Porter, our player development coach, was in here every day with her when she came here.

"She came in early, in here every day, continuing to work, continuing to grind, continuing to push. You know, she's not focused on anything outside of herself for where she is right now. When you watch KK work, she's working on all the things that we need her to be great in right now for this team for this year, and you see the result of it and our staff and the commitment that we have to continuing to pour into her to continue to hold her accountable and for her for being so coachable.

"She's a great template and a great resource for young players."

articles.summary: NBA News: Minnesota traded Josh Green and cash to Utah for Cody Williams and John Konchar on Friday night, per ESPN's Shams Charania. The move frees roughly $14.
articles.body: Minnesota traded Josh Green and cash to Utah for Cody Williams and John Konchar on Friday night, per ESPN's Shams Charania. The move frees roughly $14.7 million in salary, enough for the Wolves to officially sign Jonathan Kuminga to a two-year, $12.4 million deal via the taxpayer midlevel exception. Minnesota plans to waive-and-stretch Konchar's $6.2 million contract over three seasons and keep Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024.Tim Connelly needed to clear a specific number, and Josh Green's expiring contract was the cleanest way to do it. Minnesota sent Green and cash to Utah for Cody Williams and John Konchar, a trade built entirely around making room to sign Jonathan Kuminga through the taxpayer midlevel exception.Green's $14.7 million deal was the realistic piece to move. Without a trade, the Wolves' fallback was stretching Green's own money at a cost of nearly $5 million in dead cap over three years. Instead, they moved him outright and absorbed a smaller, calculated hit elsewhere.CategoryPlayerCurrent TeamContract StatusSalary Cap HitOutgoing (MIN)Josh GreenUtah Jazz (incoming)Expiring$14.7 millionIncoming (MIN)Cody WilliamsMinnesota (incoming)Rookie scale, $7.67M team option for 2027-28~$6.5 million/yearIncoming (MIN)John KoncharWaived, to be stretchedN/A$6.2 million (stretched to ~$2.05M/year over 3 years)Why Minnesota needed the money to moveShams Charania wrote: "The Minnesota Timberwolves are trading Josh Green and cash to the Utah Jazz for Cody Williams and John Konchar, sources tell ESPN."Konchar, a 30-year-old rebounding specialist, doesn't fit a crowded wing rotation in Minnesota. He'll be waived and his $6.2 million salary stretched across three seasons, creating roughly $2 million a year in dead cap instead of one lump hit. That maneuver, combined with moving Green's money, is what actually unlocks the Kuminga signing.Utah's side: Perimeter defense now, a project for laterFor the Jazz, it's a straightforward add. He joins Josh Okogie, signed this summer, as another defensive-minded wing.Cody Williams goes the other way as the bigger swing. The younger brother of Jalen Williams struggled through two lottery-pick seasons in Utah, shooting 21.4 percent from three last year. But his defense improved late in the season, enough that ESPN's Zach Lowe said "there's a world in which he's a functional eighth to tenth guy" on a good roster. SB Nation's SLC Dunk named him Utah's second-most-improved player of the year.Minnesota now has 14 players under contract with all three two-way spots filled, leaving one open roster spot. articles.title: T-Wolves Reportedly Trade For Former Top-10 NBA Draft Pick After Jonathan Kuminga Contract
articles.summary: On the heels of their contract agreement with Jonathan Kuminga, the Minnesota Timberwolves have made a trade to clear cap space and add more depth to their backcourt.
articles.body:
On the heels of their contract agreement with Jonathan Kuminga, the Minnesota Timberwolves have made a trade to clear cap space and add more depth to their backcourt.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania , the Timberwolves are acquiring former top-10 pick Cody Williams and John Konchar from the Utah Jazz for Josh Green and cash.

Charania and The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski reported the Wolves plan to waive Konchar.

Lakers' Top Targets After Kuminga Miss 🎯

A move was expected from Minnesota because it didn't have the necessary cap space available to add Kuminga's two-year, $12.4 million contract and stay out of the second apron.

Green, who was acquired from the Charlotte Hornets as part of the LaMelo Ball trade, made the most sense as a trade candidate because he is playing the 2026-27 season on a $14.7 million expiring contract.

The Jazz needed another wing who can play off the bench or step into the starting lineup if Lauri Markkanen misses time due to injuries. Green is also an effective three-point shooter with a 38.7 percent success rate on a low volume in his career.

Williams and Konchar are combining to make roughly $12.2 million this season. By waiving and stretching Konchar's contract, the Timberwolves can pay out his $6.2 million salary over the next three years instead of one lump sum in 2026-27.

The T-Wolves were $4.1 million under the second apron before this trade. They were able to create the some additional financial wiggle room while taking a flyer on a recent lottery pick with upside.

Williams, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft, took a step forward in his second season with 8.8 points and 3.0 rebounds per game in 67 appearances (41 starts) for the Jazz.

Minnesota will slot Williams into a bench role behind Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu to fill out its wing rotation.

Given the financial restrictions and limited draft capital they operated with, Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly has done a good job of reshaping this roster around Anthony Edwards in an attempt to take a step forward coming off a second-round playoff loss to the San Antonio Spurs last season.

articles.title: Ja Morant Reacts to Damian Lillard's Photo of Incredible Performance in Practice Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: Portland Trail Blazers star Damian Lillard's recent performance during a practice session caught the attention of many people, including new teammate Ja Morant.
articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers star Damian Lillard's recent performance during a practice session caught the attention of many people, including new teammate Ja Morant.

After Lillard posted a photo showing he made 1,100 out of 1,168 shot attempts, Morant reacted with a simple comment stating "this gon be funnnnn".

Lillard has not played in an NBA game since April 27, 2025, when he was with the Milwaukee Bucks. He tore his Achilles in Game 4 of the first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, then was surprisingly waived by the Bucks just over a month later with $113 million remaining on his contract.

The move opened the door for Lillard to return to the Blazers, with whom he spent the first 11 years of his NBA career and became one of the best players of this generation.

Morant is joining Portland this season after being acquired in a trade with the Memphis Grizzlies.

The pairing of Lillard and Morant gives the Blazers one of the most intriguing backcourt duos if they stay healthy. They have combined to play a total of 128 games over the past two seasons.

Portland has one of the most fascinating rosters in the NBA right now. Lillard, Morant, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson are all in the backcourt. Deni Avdija is coming off a breakout season that earned him an All-Star nod. Donovan Clingan was one of the league's best rebounders and rim protectors last season.

All of these pieces suggest a team that could be very good, but they have the difficult test of playing in the Western Conference with arguably the two best teams in the NBA in the San Antonio Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder.

articles.title: From spit on to hugged, Riley Gaines unlocks main problem with the WNBA, and it’s as simple as red vs blue
articles.summary: Riley Gaines received hugs and smiles at an Indiana Fever game after being booed in Minneapolis, highlighting the red state-blue state divide in the WNBA.
articles.body: What a difference a red state makes. Unapologetic and steadfast, Riley Gaines, the nation’s leading advocate for the preservation of women’s sports for biological women, gets under the skin of woke leftists without even trying. She travels the country, and says that biological men don’t belong. The audacity! THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID In some places in this country, Gaines gets booed for speaking this simple logic and truth. She gets yelled at. Even spit on for her beliefs. That was the kind of reception Gaines got at her very first WNBA game in Minneapolis earlier this summer, when she dared to take a sign into the arena that praised Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham for bravely speaking up for girls in girls' sports. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS RALLY IN INDIANA WHILE DISPLAYING WHAT MAKES AMERICA GREAT Fast-forward to her second-ever WNBA game, Friday night in Indianapolis at an Indiana Fever game in which former NBA player Royce White (now sometimes going by "Roysha") made a surprise appearance, and Gaines got a much different reception. Hugs, smiles, requests for photographs. ROYCE WHITE SHOWS UP TO INDIANA FEVER GAME IN BLONDE WIG AMID WNBA DRAFT PURSUIT Blue state, red state. Delusional, sensible. Hostile, friendly. Perhaps this is part of the problem with the powder keg that is the WNBA. There are 15 teams in the league, and only two are located in solid red states: the Indiana Fever and the Dallas Wings. Atlanta, Las Vegas and Phoenix have teams, but those states aren’t reliably red, more purple. The league is adding Cleveland in 2028, so that might help, but the scale will still be far from balanced. "My main takeaway is that when Minneapolis is booing you, it’s generally a good sign," Gaines told OutKick with a bit of tongue-in-cheek during halftime of Friday’s game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, which the Fever won easily over the Connecticut Sun, 111-91. "Especially for those of us with common sense and an ounce of integrity and a shred of honesty." If there were people in the Fever crowd on Friday that were more Minneapolis than Indianapolis, you wouldn’t know it. Just a different atmosphere and decorum altogether. And that fuels Gaines. The poor reception in Minneapolis didn’t deter her at all. Knowing that so many people across the United States agree with her does. On Friday, as she supported Cunningham and White, Gaines proudly sported a black T-shirt with neon green XX-XY lettering, a label so controversial in some (blue!) WNBA cities that fans at an Atlanta Dream game were recently asked to cover that same shirt. STEPHANIE WHITE, LET ME 'EDUCATE' YOU ON THE SCIENCE OF WHY MEN DON'T BELONG IN WOMEN'S SPORTS The nonsense on gender in the WNBA is incessant. And neither White nor Enes Kanter Freedom could stand to sit back and watch it a second longer. Earlier this month, White joined Freedom, another former NBA star, in saying that they now identify as trans women while also declaring their interest in joining the WNBA next year via the 2027 WNBA Draft. Freedom and White decided to fight lunacy with lunacy, using their over-the-top declarations as a way to push back on the WNBA’s lack of spine and clarity in the trans in women’s sports dilemma. If the WNBA can’t define a woman, can’t put clear language into its bylaws that limits participation in the league to strictly biological women, then Freedom and White say that they will take this fight as far as they can. They say that trying to play in the WNBA isn’t talk, that they are prepared to walk that walk if necessary. They are also prepared to fight through litigation if necessary. While Freedom was ejected from a WNBA game he attended last week in blue Chicago (Sky player Natasha Cloud sniped at him during the game, he responded, fans booed him, and he was ultimately permanently banned from Wintrust Arena), White was received warmly in red Indiana. No boos. No yelling. Instead, fans approached White with smiles and respect and outstretched arms for handshakes and fist bumps. They asked for photos. They thanked him, told him they loved what he is doing for women's sports. "You can't expect that, it was overwhelming," White told OutKick, regarding his Indiana welcome. "But...I think people have a lot of appreciation for what Roysha is doing and some of the other people who are fighting as well. It's just so crazy to me the difference in response here in Indiana versus in Chicago (for Freedom). But one city is run by people who have common sense and the other one isn't, so there's that." Gaines received similar treatment at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. "Let me tell you the difference, being here in Indiana, a home game for the Fever," Gaines said. "The looks that you’re getting are smiles, people are winking. People are coming up and saying thank you. People are expressing their gratitude for the stance that I (have taken). "Not the same response I had in Minneapolis." Gaines expects nothing less from blue cities and blue states now. She understands her messaging in those areas requires her to bring a much stiffer upper lip, and an extra layer of Teflon coating. And even though that's expected, it's not always easy, which is why she so deeply respects and appreciates what Freedom and White are doing. Gaines and White talked at length at halftime of Friday’s game about their convictions on the trans in women’s sports dilemma. Gaines said that it is ironic that WNBA players like Cloud from the Chicago Sky are missing the point of what Freedom and White are trying to do. "I was watching the altercation between Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha (Cloud) where obscenities were yelled back and forth, at least on Natasha’s end at Enes, and I thought to myself, ultimately, Natasha really should be thanking Enes, because what he’s fighting for…is her," Gaines said. "He is fighting for her to have the opportunity and the ability to achieve and to exceed in her sport and even beyond." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Others besides White and Freedom are fighting alongside Gaines for the very same thing. The Indiana Attorney General, Todd Rokita, who sat with Gaines and her husband during Friday's game, has been active in trying to protect girls and women in sports. "I’m pleased to host my friend Riley Gaines tonight with her husband and we’re having a good time," Rokita told OutKick. "But the fact of the matter is, there are a lot of leaders in this country who see the obvious, and the obvious is that sports teams should only have the same biological sex because there are differences. And I am so happy that these biological men (Freedom and White) are proving the point when they are coming to apply for the WNBA solely because the WNBA can’t get its own bylaws straight." What is happening in the WNBA, with the ambiguity surrounding eligibility, concerns Rokita because it could just as easily happen elsewhere, which creates a slippery slope. "As Indiana’s Attorney General, I am looking at this very closely, from the perspective of whether you are for-profit or non-profit, the fact that you have bylaws that make sense and comply with all laws and that they are clear and non-abusive," Rokita said. "And if you can’t define in your bylaws what a woman is and who’s eligible to be on your teams, you’re entering a real gray area in terms of law, in terms of being abusive or deceptive to those you serve. "If the WNBA can’t make some simple decisions about what their bylaws should read, you may see a lot of states, a lot of my friends, get involved, including Indiana." Now wouldn’t that be something? How ironic if it is a couple of men pretending to be women, along with red-state fans and politicians, who ultimately save the very woke and leftist and blue WNBA from itself. It really could be as simple as that. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Does the WNBA need more red-state teams? Let me know at: patricia.babcockmcgraw@outkick.com

articles.title: Knicks' Josh Hart Jokes About Reputation After Offseason Workout Video, 'Delete This'
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Josh Hart joked that clips of him practicing this offseason will spoil his reputation as what Jalen Brunson has described as "the worst practice player" in the NBA.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Josh Hart joked that clips of him practicing this offseason will spoil his reputation as what Jalen Brunson has described as "the worst practice player" in the NBA.

Hart responded Saturday to a video of him putting up shots at the Bridgehampton School in New York.

"Yo delete this," Hart wrote. "I need to keep the perception that I don't workout in the summer!"

Kevin Durant addresses viral paparazzi picture

Both Brunson and coach Mike Brown called out Hart's practice habits in a June 30 episode of Brunson and Hart's podcast The Roommates Show.

"I don't think he's had one good practice day this year... you're the worst practice player ever," Brunson told Hart around the 45:00 mark of the podcast. "That goes back to 'Nova... if any other player in the league did that, they'd be waived."

Brown added Hart was given "by far" the longest leash of any star player on his team.

Hart's practice habits didn't get in the way of him joining his former Villanova teammates Brunson and Mikal Bridges in helping lead the Knicks to the 2026 NBA title.

The Knicks, which lost Mitchell Robinson but added Andre Drummond this summer, have about a month left before their title defense begins with the start of training camp.

articles.title: Sparks' Cameron Brink is making a late awards push with great string of performances
articles.summary: Brink is gaining valuable experience amid LA's lost season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Sparks entered 2026 intent on making a playoff push and ending a five-year postseason drought.

Though the Sparks didn't meet that goal and ended up trading franchise point guard Kelsey Plum earlier this month, Los Angeles has gotten a better look at its future -- which should include third-year big Cameron Brink.

Brink is making a late push for Sixth Player of the Year consideration amid a string of strong recent performances. The former second overall pick is reminding viewers why she was coveted so highly coming out of Stanford in 2024, when the Sparks selected her just behind Caitlin Clark.

Injuries and the Sparks' uncertain direction have hampered Brink's development, but she is carving out an important role in Los Angeles. She reaffirmed that position in helping the Sparks to an 88-82 upset win over the playoff-bound Washington Mystics on Friday.

In 26 minutes, Brink scored 13 points, hauled in five rebounds and recorded two blocks. Over the past five games in which she has played 20 minutes or more, Brink is averaging 12.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.2 blocks.

For the first time, Brink is shooting better than 50 percent from the floor, and her 33.8 success rate from 3-point range also is a career-best.

The Sparks might have only four wins from their past 18 games, but the second half of 2026 has given Los Angeles valuable insight into what its next core should look like.

That core should include Brink, who -- when healthy -- is more than worth counting on.

articles.title: Fever’s Stephanie White compares Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell to historic duo
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell continue to set records as a dynamic duo, leading up to Fever coach Stephanie White's comparison for them.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell dominated with another historic performance in the Indiana Fever's blowout win over the Connecticut Sun on Friday night. Their efforts ended up getting a legendary comparison from head coach Stephanie White.

Clark finished with a stat line of 34 points, 12 assists, five rebounds, and three steals. On the other hand, Mitchell produced 34 points, four assists, three rebounds, and one steal. They also scored or assisted on 92 of the team's 111 points, the third most in a game in WNBA history, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. They set the record against the Chicago Sky with 98 on Aug. 23.

White marveled at the combined talent of her star duo after the game, per ESPN. The Fever coach even went as far to say that they reminded her of Diana Taurasi and Cappie Pondexter, who helped lead the Phoenix Mercury to WNBA titles in 2007 and 2009.

"You think back to those Phoenix days, like they were a dynamic backcourt that could put up big numbers, could both get their own shot, could get other people involved," White said. "But it's been a long time since we've seen the explosiveness of two players like what Kelsey and Caitlin have been doing, and doing it with remarkable consistency."

How Caitlin Clark and Fever Played Against Sun

Four players scored in double-digits for Indiana in the win over Connecticut, including Clark and Mitchell. Aliyah Boston came next with 14 points and two rebounds, while Makayla Timpson provided 10 points and eight rebounds.

Indiana improved to a 26-14 record on the season, sitting at first place in the Eastern Conference standings. They are above the Atlanta Dream and the New York Liberty at the moment.

articles.title: Say goodbye to college football Week 0
articles.summary: One of the strangest scheduling anomalies in all of sports is about to have its swan song this weekend in college football’s befuddling and charming Week 0....
articles.body:
One of the strangest scheduling anomalies in all of sports is about to have its swan song this weekend in college football's befuddling and charming Week 0.

The fact that a Week 0 even exists is quintessential college football in that it couldn't really exist anywhere else and make any sense at all. However, it has been alive for years, allowing a select handful of teams an opportunity to begin the regular season a week before everybody else. The weekend is open to anyone playing an international game (TCU-UNC in Dublin, Ireland) and anyone playing an away game at Hawaii to compensate for their extra travel. The NCAA can also provide a waiver for games, although that is rare. This season, it was given to NC State and Virginia as they were originally scheduled to play their season opener in Brazil before it was moved back stateside .

However, 2026 will be the last year that the sport enjoys an appetizer before the regular season truly kicks off in full. The FBS Oversight Committee approved legislation on Friday that will move the calendar up one week so that all teams begin during the week that has served as Week 0.

"Earlier this year, the FBS Calendar Subgroup presented recommendations to the committee to amend the regular season and the off-campus recruiting model," the NCAA briefing said. "In response to those recommendations, a new FBS first-contest date has been adopted and will take effect in the 2027 season. The season will begin on the Thursday of what is now designated Week 0 and end on the Saturday after Thanksgiving."

This year's Week 0 consists of eight games. And while none of them are true barnburners, it's a nice, gentle way to start the regular season. And with American fans starved for any kind of football that matters, we will gladly sit down and watch New Mexico State travel to Florida State in primetime.

The switch allows for college football to have an extra full week during the NFL preseason, which will only serve to help get the sport more attention and higher ratings as it begins its campaign. Week 0 did provide some decent options for television windows, but the networks likely won't complain about one more week of a full slate of games. It would also allow teams an extra bye week during the year to get more rest and spread out their schedules.

It's a sensible change from the NCAA, which is really saying something considering that the governing body for college athletics hasn't done much, as their world exists in a state of total chaos. To be sure, there are many other calendar issues to be sorted out, like the CFP going late into January and the ridiculousness of the transfer portal. But at least this is one step in the right direction, even if we will miss our quirky and beloved tradition of Week 0.

articles.title: New York Mets reinstate slugger Juan Soto from the 10-day injured list
articles.summary: New York Mets slugger Juan Soto was reinstated from the 10-day injured list on Saturday ahead of the team's game against the Houston Astros.  The five-time A...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — New York Mets slugger Juan Soto was reinstated from the 10-day injured list on Saturday ahead of the team's game against the Houston Astros.

The five-time All-Star landed on the injured list last month for the second time this season after imaging revealed a grade 2 strain.

Soto had been nursing the nagging calf problem for about a week before he left a game against the Dodgers in discomfort. He walked twice against Los Angeles starter Roki Sasaki during a 4-2 loss at Citi Field before being replaced by pinch-hitter Jorge Polanco in the sixth inning with the score tied at 1.

Soto is hitting .283 with 21 homers, 52 RBIs and a .947 OPS in 84 games during his second season with the Mets.

The Mets also optioned infielder Eric Wagaman to Triple-A following Friday night's 3-1 loss to the Astros .

articles.title: Stephanie White Details Major Similarity Between Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Iconic WNBA Championship-Winning Duo
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever have already secured their spot in the 2026 WNBA playoffs, but they are showing no signs of slowing down. On Saturday, the Fever picked up...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have already secured their spot in the 2026 WNBA playoffs, but they are showing no signs of slowing down. On Saturday, the Fever picked up their 26th win of the year after defeating the Connecticut Sun 111-91.

However, it was not just the result that caught attention. After the game, head coach Stephanie White made a special comparison between Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell and one of the most memorable backcourts in WNBA history.

Stephanie White's Unique Comparison of Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell

During the postgame press conference, The Athletic's James Boyd asked White what it was like to watch the growing chemistry between Clark and Mitchell and whether another backcourt duo came to mind when she watched them play.

"The only other two that I can think of off the top of my head are Diana Taurasi and Cappie Pondexter. I mean, when you think back to those Phoenix days, like they were a dynamic backcourt that could put up big numbers."

"Could both get their own shot, could get other people involved. But it's been a long time since we've seen the explosiveness of two players like Kelsey and Caitlin have been doing, and been doing it with remarkable consistency," White said .

Taurasi and Pondexter were a major part of the Mercury team that won the WNBA championship in 2007 and 2009.

During the 2009 championship season, Pondexter led the league with 648 points, while Taurasi finished second with 631. Now, years later, Clark and Mitchell are putting together a similar partnership in Indiana.

They showed exactly why White made the comparison against Connecticut. Both players finished with 34 points, combining for 68 of Indiana's 111 points. Clark also added 12 assists, while Mitchell added four assists.

Interestingly, the game did not start well for the Fever. Connecticut came out strong, and Indiana trailed 28-19 after the first quarter.

That quickly changed. Clark and Mitchell helped spark the comeback as the Fever turned the point deficit into a 58-43 halftime lead. Indiana scored 39 points in the second quarter, completely changing the pace of the game.

The Fever will now get some time away from regular-season action before returning to the court. Their next game is scheduled for September 18 against the Toronto Tempo.

articles.body: No satisfecho con haber dinamitado el mercado europeo, el Dubái Basketball también pesca en canteras. Él acabó con unas bestiales medias de 28,5 puntos, 13,0 rebotes y 36,3 créditos de valoración. También ayudó a Aragón a conseguir la tercera plaza en el Campeonato de España de Selecciones Autonómicas. La de Keita es una incorporación de futuro de un Dubái Basketball que ha sumado para su plantilla a grandes nombres como los de Elie Okobo, Jaron Blossomgame, Tornike Shengelia, Mamadi Diakite y Davion Mintz. Junto a la incorporación de Xavi Pascual en el banquillo, y sumados a lo que ya había, el conjunto de los emiratos se ha convertido en serio aspirante a disputar la Final Four de la Euroliga. Ha apostado fuerte de cara al presente, pero también se ha movido pensando en el futuro. Así, se ha hecho también con el verdinegro Yannick Kraag, que seguirá cedido en el Asisa Joventut; Simonas Lukosius, que jugará en el Unicaja, y Kevin Kokila, que recalará en la Virtus. articles.title: Natasha Cloud Dismisses Enes Kanter Freedom as Sky Ban Him from Home Games
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Natasha Cloud didn't want to waste time and energy talking about Enes Kanter Freedom on Saturday as she prepared for the Chicago Sky's game against the New York Liberty.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Natasha Cloud didn't want to waste time and energy talking about Enes Kanter Freedom on Saturday as she prepared for the Chicago Sky's game against the New York Liberty.

"I won't be talking about anything that happened with an irrelevant person," Cloud said. "What I will focus on is what actually affects women and children currently in 2026."

Cloud then went on to name domestic violence, sexual assault and food insecurities as three things that women are most affected by.

Cloud got into a confrontation with Freedom at last Sunday's Chicago home game against the Indiana Fever. The former NBA player was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female." The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then chest bumped with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Freedom's direction.

The 34-year-old Cloud started yelling and pointing at Freedom as she approached him. He stood, held his arms out and stepped onto the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved between the two.

"I will not talk about an irrelevant threat to our lives because that's exactly what it is," she said. "I want to talk about real issues that face women, and it's not our trans human beings, and it's not our drag queens. It's not our gay community. There is a certain demographic of people that you can generally search. It's a simple Google search of what is the greatest threat to women and children currently in 2026, in the United States of America."

Freedom has been banned by Sky owner Michael Alter from attending any future Chicago home games.

Cloud applauded the move by the front office to "protect the players."

"That's what protection looks like on the whole. I want everyone to hear that," she said. "That's what protection looks like from the right."

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told The Associated Press on Monday that they are not eligible . The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the situation.

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.

Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

"We won't allow our league to be used as a pawn for any political or cultural wars that the right wants," Cloud said. "We're absolutely not going to. This league has always stood on principle and on our humanitarian efforts."

Cloud wished the talk was about the amazing season the WNBA has been having on the court with strong ratings — that game against Indiana drew 3.3 million viewers , which was the most since the league's inaugural season in 1997.

"I just had a fan who identifies as trans cry to me in here and this is why I do what I do," Cloud said. "None of this is performative. I don't want to put myself in front of fires all the time. I don't want to be the one that always has to speak up. But somebody (expletive) has to do it."

articles.title: KCP's Wife Reveals Philadelphia Apartment Struck by Lightning in Video Right After Signing Lease
articles.summary: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope apparently received a jarring welcome to his new city after signing this summer with the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Kentavious Caldwell-Pope apparently received a jarring welcome to his new city after signing this summer with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Caldwell-Pope's wife McKenzie said in video posted Friday to her TikTok the couple's penthouse unit was struck by lightning minutes after she signed a lease in Philadelphia.

According to McKenzie, the strike sounded like a loud bang followed by water pouring through cracks in the ceiling.

Kevin Durant addresses viral paparazzi picture

McKenzie added she fled the apartment by descending 14 flights of stairs because the strike had knocked out the building's elevators.

McKenzie added she had been told by an electrician there was a 1 in 400 million chance of an apartment unit getting struck like the Caldwell-Popes'.

Caldwell-Pope, who played key roles in championship runs with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 and Denver Nuggets in 2023, spent last season with the Memphis Grizzlies.

He averaged 8.4 points through 51 games before he was shut down for the season after undergoing February surgery on his right pinkie.

Caldwell-Pope will hope to receive better luck in terms of both health and home as he gears up for his first season as a depth option in a backcourt led by Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

articles.title: 2026 WNBA Playoffs Bracket Picture, Standings As Sabrina Ionescu, Liberty Battle for Seeding
articles.summary: It has been something of an up-and-down season for the New York Liberty, but they are heading to the playoffs for the sixth year in a row.
articles.body:
It has been something of an up-and-down season for the New York Liberty, but they are heading to the playoffs for the sixth year in a row.

New York clinched a spot in the postseason last Sunday night thanks to the Washington Mystics' win over the Portland Fire.

The Liberty are in a tight battle for seeding in the playoff bracket and are currently in the sixth seed in the WNBA standings after a Saturday win against the Chicago Sky.

If they remain in the sixth seed, the Liberty could be in store for a first-round matchup against the Las Vegas Aces, which are currently third.

Expectations are always high in New York with star power such as Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones, as well as a recent track record that includes back-to-back WNBA Finals appearances in 2023 and 2024 and the championship in the second of those appearances.

They were high once again coming into the 2026 campaign, and they went nowhere when the Liberty got off to a red-hot 11-4 start. However, they went 2-8 in their next 10 games to fall all the way to 13-12.

The cold streak ended any realistic chance New York had to compete for the top seed and the home-court advantage that comes with it, although the team at least won the Commissioner's Cup with a victory over the Las Vegas Aces during that stretch.

It was a reminder of how dangerous the Liberty can be against any opponent when playing at their best, and they have been closer to that version of themselves of late with a 11-4 record since falling to 13-12.

With the trio of Stewart, Ionescu and Jones leading the way, New York is still a threat to reach the WNBA Finals regardless of what seed it ends up with in the playoff bracket.

All three playmakers have championships on their resume and the ability to take over a game at a moment's notice. Throw in the overall positional versatility with Ionescu directing the offense from the perimeter, Stewart making plays on the wing and Jones battling down low, and there is a lot for opposing defenses to deal with on a nightly basis.

Given their position in the standings, the Liberty are surely going to have to win some clutch games on the road if they are going to capture the WNBA title.

But they have the talent to do just that after clinching yet another playoff appearance.

articles.title: Yahoo! runs embarrassing error in headline, proving even media outlets need time to round into midseason form
articles.summary: Yahoo! Sports mistakenly labeled Northwestern State a Big Ten team after Louisiana Christian's historic NAIA upset in the college football opener.
articles.body: College football may indeed be back in our lives, but after more than eight months of inactivity, it's normal to experience some rust. The first game of the FBS season between TCU and North Carolina certainly featured its fair share of penalties and sloppy play, which is to be expected in a season opener, especially one that's being played an entire ocean away. But that sloppiness and rust doesn't just apply to the players, either. ESPN PERSONALITY BUSTED ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR INACCURATELY TRYING TO PROMOTE THE SEC'S STRENGTH OF SCHEDULE We've all heard the phrase "it’s preseason for the refs too," and even fans can fall victim to some early-season cobwebs, including slow channel-changing reaction times and an intolerance to junk food. Media outlets aren't immune to this phenomenon either, as one famous outlet showed us on Friday. After Louisiana Christian took down Northwestern State, the internet was abuzz, and not just because it was one of the first college football games of the 2026 season. LCU is a lowly NAIA team, and on Thursday evening, they became the first team of that classification to take down a Division I opponent. Northwestern State resides in the FCS, which is a rung below the FBS level that teams like Ohio State and Alabama play in, but the accomplishment is still historic and noteworthy. Someone forgot to tell one of the writers at Yahoo! Sports, however, as they ran a headline labeling Northwestern State as a "Big Ten team." The site took the article down, as clicking the link will take you to an error page, but fortunately for all of us, the internet is forever, and one eagle-eyed fan on X spotted the error before Yahoo! could react. That's embarrassing. On one hand, I get it. You're working on a tight deadline and you need to get your story out right away, so sometimes you'll make a mistake or two (Lord knows I've been there before). But getting Northwestern confused with Northwestern State is a pretty egregious blunder, especially if you fancy yourself a "sports outlet." THE ATHLETIC PROBES DIANNA RUSSINI AND MIKE VRABEL RELATIONSHIP WHILE CONSIDERING GETTING IN BED WITH THE NFL And this doesn't just fall on the writer, either — whose name I won't include because I don't want to make them feel worse than I'm sure they already do — because this presumably made it past a couple editors too. How did no one catch the headline for a full 24 hours? I checked, and in the time I started writing this story, the article went from being live to disappearing. It took a guy with 13,000 followers on X to catch a mistake that should have been squashed in the editing process. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It's not a good look for Yahoo! Sports, but i guess even media outlets need time to round into midseason form.

articles.title: La era Pedro Martínez en el Real Madrid arranca con derrota
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, con las bajas de siete internacionales, caen en un amistoso ante el Río Breogán en el estreno del técnico
articles.summary: Los blancos, con las bajas de siete internacionales, caen en un amistoso ante el Río Breogán en el estreno del técnico
articles.body: La 'era Pedro Martínez' en el Real Madrid arrancó en Pontevedra con una derrota frente al Breogán (110-102), en el partido que supuso la vuelta de Walter Tavares cuatro meses después de su lesión, y en el que su equipo acabó sucumbiendo ante el acierto exterior de su rival, liderado por Francis Alonso, Peris y un Víctor Arteaga que llegó un contrato temporal y está reclamando uno de mayor duración. Pese a no contar con cuatro de sus caras nuevas -Mikael Jantunen, Jaime Pradilla, Max Shulga y Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot- y tres jugadores llamados a asumir un papel protagonista en el equipo -Facundo Campazzo, Gabriel Deck y Andrés Feliz-, el nuevo Real Madrid de Pedro Martínez ya enseñó su identidad en el primer amistoso de la pretemporada. Este Real Madrid poco se parecerá al de Sergio Scariolo. Su nuevo entrenador apuesta por un ritmo altísimo, y ante el Breogán quedó claro: los blancos intentarán correr para castigar a la defensa rival cada vez que puedan -al descanso firmaron 15 puntos en acciones de contraataque-. La otra gran noticia estuvo en la vuelta de Walter Tavares, quien renunció a estar con su selección en esta 'ventana FIBA' para acelerar su puesta a punto. El pívot caboverdiano no jugaba desde que a finales de abril se dañó la rodilla izquierda en el primer encuentro de la serie de cuartos de final de la Euroliga ante el Hapoel Tel Aviv. Su presencia en la pintura fue una amenaza para el Breogán, pese a que todavía está lejos de su nivel. Tavares alcanzó el descanso con 9 puntos y 4 rebotes, para una valoración de 12 créditos, la misma que firmó el pívot francés Olivier Sarr en 12 minutos gracias a sus nueve rebotes. Pese al 2-4 de salida favorable a los blancos, el Breogán siempre dominó el electrónico. Entre Francis Alonso, Aranitovic y Víctor Arteaga marcaron el ritmo anotador del equipo lucense, que no acusó las importantes bajas de los internacionales Danko Brankovic, Aleksa Ilic, Dominik Mavra y Jonathan Kasibabu. En el arranque del tercer asalto, el Breogán recuperó la renta de diez puntos que ya había gozado en la primera parte tras un parcial 9-0 (48-38). Francis Alonso, con dos triples seguidos, uno acompañado de un tiro adicional, disparó a los gallegos (62-52, min.23). El Real Madrid, moviendo con mucha fluidez el balón, se acercó en el marcador (64-60). Dos triples prácticamente seguidos de Peris oxigenaron al Breogán (71-63, min.27), pero su rival ya había metido una marcha a su juego. Con un triple sobre la bocina del joven Pablo Mera, los blancos culminaron su remontada (78-79, min.30). En el inicio del último cuarto, el Breogán, explotando su acierto exterior, golpeó nuevamente a los de Pedro Martínez, quien, muy enfadado por las concesiones defensivas de los suyos, paró el choque con un tiempo muerto (96-87, min.35). Con una mejoría defensiva y después de un triple de Okeke, el Real Madrid se acercó a tres (105-102), pero los gallegos aguantaron el arreón blanco para sumar su segunda victoria en otros tantos partidos en esta pretemporada. 110 Río Breogán (26+25+27+32): Tevin Brown (6), Bolton (13), Francis Alonso (20), Andric (11) y Arteaga (19) -cinco inicial- Josep Peris (19), Tamba (4), Aranitovic (12), Erik Quintela (2) Edgar Vicedo (4) y Néstor Viño. 102 Real Madrid (22+24+33+23): Sergio Llull (5), Pablo Mera (5), Procida (16), Okeke (18) y Tavares (17) -cinco inicial- Robinson (-), Alberto Abalde (10), Maledon (15), Ndiaye (10) y Olivier Sarr (6). Árbitros: Martín Caballero, Alfonso Olivares y Raúl Zamorano. Incidencias: Encuentro amistoso correspondiente a la segunda edición del 'Dream Game' disputado en el pabellón municipal de Pontevedra ante unos 2.500 espectadores.

articles.title: Nets rookies Mikel Brown Jr., Joshua Jefferson choose numbers
articles.summary: Brooklyn Nets rookies Mikel Brown Jr. and Joshua Jefferson have chosen their numbers for the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets are about one month away from beginning their preparations for the upcoming 2026-27 NBA season after finishing last year with a lowly 20-62 record. Brooklyn will be relying on their players that they selected in the 2026 NBA Draft to step up on the court as the team tries to win as many games as possible and two of them have chosen their numbers.

In a photo posted on the Nets ' X social media account, rookies Mikel Brown Jr. and Joshua Jefferson posed with No. 0 and No. 9 jerseys, respectively, prior to both participating in the summer circuit. Brown was able to play in the California Classic and Las Vegas Summer League once the team felt comfortable with him taking the floor amidst his recovery from a back injury while Jefferson had to wait until Las Vegas to step on the court.

Jefferson, whom the Nets selected with the No. 28 overall pick in the 2026 draft, was only able to put on a Nets jersey because of a trade from the Minnesota Timberwolves that netted Brooklyn the No. 28 pick and forward Julius Randle. The trade bringing Randle and Jefferson to the Nets was not finalized until midway through the Las Vegas Summer League so the rookie's debut took longer than expected.

Jefferson, 22 , showed some flashes during his time in Las Vegas as he averaged 7.3 points, 1.7 rebounds, 1.3 assists, and 2.0 steals per game while shooting 33.3% from the field and 12.5% from behind the three-point line. Jefferson displayed his ability to handle the ball in a 6-foot-9, 240-pound body while also showing that he has some areas of his game to work on before next season comes around.

Brown, 20 , had a solid performance for the Nets across the California Classic and Las Vegas Summer League as he had some awe-inspiring moments with the ball in his hands. In four games played in Brooklyn's summer circuit, Brown averaged 15.0 points, 1.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists, and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 38.8% from the floor and 34.6% from deep.

articles.title: Royce White became a fan-favorite guest at Fever game amid Simone Biles' appearance
articles.summary: Royce White showed up unannounced to Friday's Indiana Fever game and was mobbed by fans, a stark contrast to Enes Kanter Freedom's Chicago ejection.
articles.body: On a night when Simone Biles was in the building, Indiana Fever fans flocked to Royce White. White, a former NBA player who became a viral sensation after declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft, showed up at Friday night’s Fever game in what he says was an unannounced appearance. White told OutKick that he didn't give the Fever any notice that he would be coming, and the ticket wasn't even purchased under his name. The Fever have not responded to requests for comment. FORMER NBA PLAYER ROYCE WHITE OFFICIALLY DECLARES FOR 2027 WNBA DRAFT AS LEAGUE'S CULTURE WAR CONTINUES White quickly became the story of the night, as fans at Gainbridge Fieldhouse stopped to talk with him, shake his hand and take photos. The friendly reception of White was in stark contrast to how Enes Kanter Freedom was received at the Chicago Sky's home game vs. the Fever game last Sunday. Fans heckled Freedom on his way into the arena before he was ejected from the game in the third quarter. The Sky were informed that Freedom would be coming hours before the game, and team owner Michael Alter told OutKick that security was alerted of Freedom's presence at that game. White, who says the Fever had no such notice he would be showing up Friday, avoided any similar issues to Freedom. The Indiana home crowd truly embraced White. "They don't have hate for Black trans lesbians here in Indiana, it's a beautiful thing," White told OutKick after the game. "The reception was great. That's really the cool thing, juxtaposed to what Enes went through... there in Chicago. I just had a completely different experience tonight, and the people of Indiana are great." White admitted he did not expect the crowd to embrace him like that. "It's just so crazy the difference of response here in Indiana versus Chicago. But one city is run by people who have common sense and the other one isn't," he said. Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita and Riley Gaines were also at the game, and were among the other spectators who flocked to White. Gaines has her own history with Biles after they engaged in a social media spat in June 2025 over the topic of trans athletes in women's sports. But despite Gaines and Biles being in the same room together on Friday, White's presence appeared to overshadow both of them, especially in social media discussion. ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTED FROM SKY-FEVER GAME AFTER VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD Gaines, who was at her second WNBA game, also spoke about the difference in reception by fans in Indiana compared to her last outing. Gaines last attended the Fever vs Minnesota Lynx game in Minneapolis earlier this month. articles.title: Natasha Cloud calls for league-wide ban of Enes Kanter Freedom, calls culture war debate around WNBA an 'intentional distraction'
articles.summary: Kanter Freedom was kicked out of Chicago's Wintrust Arena after getting into a heated verbal exchange with Cloud during a Sky game last week.
articles.body:
After getting into a heated exchange with former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom last week, Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud says that she would like to shift the conversation.

Cloud spoke to reporters about the issue ahead of the Sky's game against the New York Liberty on Saturday. She did not refer to Kanter Freedom by name, calling him "irrelevant," but did advocate for the league to ban him from attending games.

"We're asking for protection, and that's what protection looks like from a man," Cloud said via The Athletic . "We can't not allow him in the arena before the game, but after the game, we can bring solutions to the table that best benefit putting our players first and protecting our players."

Kanter Freedom and Cloud had a heated verbal exchange during a Sky game on Sunday, which led to the former NBA player being escorted from the building. Kanter Freedom was banned from Sky home games after the incident.

Kanter Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, made headlines after attempting to challenge the WNBA's eligibility rules — though league sources have reportedly since clarified that they are not eligible .

On Saturday, Cloud commended Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca, head coach Tyler Marsh and team owner Michael Alter for their role in trying to keep the players safe.

"I hope the WNBA follows their lead," she added.

Cloud, a veteran guard who is in her 11th season in the league, has been known for being outspoken on political and social issues even before Chicago signed her to a one-year deal in May.

Cloud's outspokenness has continued this season, with the guard sounding off last week after the Sky's game against the Golden State Valkyries was interrupted by sex toys thrown on the court — the second such incident in as many days. When asked about Kanter Freedom on Saturday, though, Cloud opted to instead steer the conversation toward issues that she believes are more important.

"I won't be talking about anything that happened with an irrelevant person," Cloud said, via The Athletic. "What I will focus on is what actually affects women and children."

Cloud spoke for several minutes about multiple issues, including domestic violence, sexual assault, food insecurity and the ongoing war in the Middle East.

"I will talk about real issues that face women, and it's not our trans human beings," Cloud said, via The Athletic. "It's not our drag queens. It's not our gay community. There is a certain demographic of people that you can generally search; it's a simple Google search of what is the greatest threat to women and children in 2026 in the United States of America, and it's not going to be trans people."

Cloud added that she believes that the debate surrounding the WNBA right now is an "intentional distraction."

"The more that we hate each other, the more that we have bias against each other, the more we're going to be distracted from real life issues that are plaguing our communities," Cloud said, via Front Office Sports .

The situation has highlighted the growing issue of extremism and threats that have been targeted at WNBA players. Sky co-owner and governor Nadia Rawlinson told NPR that the team had partnered with threat intelligence company Moonshot and American University's PERIL (the Polarization and Extremism Research and Innovation Lab), with the organizations helping to monitor online threats against players and educate people on identifying and countering misogyny in the game, respectively.

When speaking on the threats on Saturday, Cloud bluntly pointed to one demographic as the "root of the issue": "Men."

"The men now that are like 'Oh, we need to protect the WNBA,' y'all were the same ones saying we shouldn't be paid," Cloud said, via The Athletic. "Y'all were the same ones saying we shouldn't have been invested in, saying we're a joke, the same ones that don't respect Black women. So, if you're going to protect women, that means all women. That includes Black women, trans women and the list goes on."

articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs forward Harrison Barnes bought a small bank in his home state of Iowa, per an exclusive interview with Paul Davis for the Bank Slate.

That prompted this insightful reaction from Indiana Pacers star (and Barnes' former Sacramento Kings teammate), Tyrese Haliburton.

Per Spotrac , Barnes has amassed career earnings of $224.1 million over his 13-year career. He's been a savvy investor over the years, if his firm, Barnes and Co., is any indication.

"Barnes & Co. mission is to protect and develop the human, intellectual, financial and social capital of the Harrison & Brittany Barnes Family. The non-indexed portion of the firm's holdings, are focused in financial services. Investments in a concentrated core of traditional financial institutions are complemented by select involvement in venture-backed B2B financial technologies."

His core investments include the following:

Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited (NTB)

Now Barnes is the owner of the Community State Bank in Paton, Iowa, per Coltrane Carlson of Raccoon Valley Radio, who spoke with Barnes about the purchase and his significant interest in banking.

"I think the biggest thing is that you have to be where your feet are," Barnes said in part.
