Barnes also spoke with Khalil Garriott of the ABA Banking Journal last June about his interest as well.

"I saw community banks act as economic first responders during COVID," Barnes said in part about what piqued his interest. "They proved to be the most effective way to distribute PPP loans and proved their value to their customers and communities."

Barnes certainly has a post-NBA path carved out, and he's already doing work on that in the present. That got Haliburton's attention on Saturday.

LINDSIDE, WV (WVNS) - It was a night of sheer purple reign at the H.E. Comer, Jr. Sports Complex in Monroe County on Friday, August 28, 2026.

Not only did the James Monroe Football team take down their rivals from down 219 in Greenbrier East in overtime, but their Girls Basketball team also got their shining moment. During halftime, the Lady Maverick players and coaching staff from last year's title run finally received their championship bling.

"It's just a wonderful feeling to be able to watch them mature throughout the year and as well through the summer. They've been waiting for these rings all summer, so. I think it's funny how important it is to them, not funny, but it is a big deal for everyone. They have earned it, certainly, and this moment here with the community and everything behind them, it means a lot to them in the future," said Head Coach Shari Helvey.

The rings are black and gold, with the James Monroe letter logo in the very center.

The Lady Mavericks had no seniors in 2025-26, and a lot of these girls have been putting in the work during the offseason in hopes of repeating. Several of them are currently suiting up for some of the other Lady Maverick sports teams, like volleyball and soccer.

articles.title: 2026 Washington basketball non-conference schedule has different look
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies men's basketball program unveiled its 2026-27 non-conference schedule on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Third-year coach Danny Sprinkle and the Washington Huskies won't be traveling far from home, outside of a flight over the Pacific Ocean, during the 2026-27 non-conference slate.

UW unveiled its entire men's basketball non-conference schedule Tuesday, featuring Big 12 Conference powers Baylor, BYU, and Utah. The Cougars will face the Huskies in the opening round of the Southwest Maui Invitational on November 23. The other two games Sprinkle's program will play in the annual basketball showcase in Hawaii are yet to be determined, but one will come against either Clemson or Ole Miss.

The Huskies are 29-35 overall and 11-29 in Big Ten Conference play over the past two seasons under Sprinkle, and will host cross-state rival Washington State for an exhibition at Alaska Airlines Arena on October 25, the first time the programs won't meet during the regular season since 1917, before tipping off the regular season against Colgate on November 2.

UW returns to the court a week later to host Mississippi Valley State of the Southwestern Athletic Conference, only the second time the two basketball programs have faced off and the first since the 2013-14 season when, under then-coach Lorenzo Romar, the Huskies came away with a 95-80 win.

Six of UW's seven non-conference games in Seattle will be at home with the other, a December 19 meeting with Baylor, being at Climate Pledge Arena. The only true road game is a November 14 trip to face Utah, the first meeting between the two former Pac-12 schools in Salt Lake City in 2023-24, a 95-90 loss to the Utes.

Sprinkle nearly checked all the Beehive State schools off his list except for his former employer, Utah State. UW comes back to Hec Edmundson Pavillion to host Utah Tech on Nov. 19 before heading out to Maui four days later to face BYU.

The Huskies close out their non-conference slate against Norfolk State (Nov. 29), Southern Utah (Dec. 8), Baylor (Dec. 19) and Cornell (Dec. 28) before opening their Big Ten schedule in January.

articles.title: Jason Kidd Reveals if He'd Return to NBA Coaching After Mavericks Exit
articles.summary: Jason Kidd confirmed that he'd be willing to coach in the NBA again following his departure from the Dallas Mavericks at the end of the 2025-26 season.
articles.body:
Jason Kidd confirmed that he'd be willing to coach in the NBA again following his departure from the Dallas Mavericks at the end of the 2025-26 season.

"Yeah, I think I love coaching. I love to watch players get better. I want to win. I want to help the team win," Kidd told Rappler's Delfin Dioquino (h/t Grant Afseth of Dallas Hoops Journal). "And so I would never say no to coaching. Maybe somewhere down the future, but also right now I'm just at home really trying to enjoy my family. And then also just watching the game and seeing if I can help others still from the coaching side. I'm always talking to Jalen Brunson and to Giannis. So just trying to help others now that I'm not coaching."

Kidd and Dallas mutually agreed to part ways on May 19 after compiling a 26-56 record during the team's 2025-26 campaign.

Kidd has spent 10 years as a head coach with the Mavericks, Milwaukee Bucks and Brooklyn Nets following his Hall of Fame career as a point guard from 1994 through 2013.

He owns a 388-395 overall record as a head coach while posting a 205-205 mark during his tenure in Dallas. Kidd helped the Mavericks make an NBA Finals appearance in 2024.

It's also worth noting that he spent multiple years as an assistant on the Los Angeles Lakers' coaching staff, including the team's 2019-20 season that ended with a championship.

Kidd is familiar with working alongside stars that include LeBron James, Luka Dončić, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jalen Brunson.

articles.title: Ranking the 5 Worst NBA Trades of the Last 5 Years
articles.summary: NBA trade analysis requires nuance. Not every deal has a clear winner or loser, and even the biggest blockbusters usually come with some level of uncertainty.
articles.body:
NBA trade analysis requires nuance. Not every deal has a clear winner or loser, and even the biggest blockbusters usually come with some level of uncertainty.

Sometimes, though, things are much simpler.

The very worst NBA trades look lopsided from the start and get even worse over time. Those are the ones we're featuring here as we try to rank the five most damaging deals of the past half-decade.

An underwhelming return package, post-trade fallout, opportunity cost—all that and more factor into what makes an NBA trade truly rotten for one side of the exchange.

Let's start at the 2021 offseason and scan the ensuing five years for the worst of the worst.

5. Lakers Acquire Russell Westbrook in 2021

The Trade: Los Angeles Lakers acquire Russell Westbrook, 2024 second-round pick and 2028 second-round pick from the Washington Wizards for Kyle Kuzma, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Montrezl Harrell and No. 22 pick in the 2021 draft

Russell Westbrook was a terrible fit on the Lakers from the moment this deal went down. Los Angeles needed shooting and defense, neither of which Russ provided.

Not so far removed from their title run in 2020, the Lakers should have given LeBron James and Anthony Davis a star who could theoretically stay on the floor during clutch moments in the playoffs. Westbrook's deficiencies kept him from being that player, and his failure to take on an alpha role that would have saved James and Davis from heavy minute totals in the regular season compounded the problem.

Westbrook who offered zero off-ball value, played inattentive defense and displayed ghastly shot-selection, actively diminishing the impact of Los Angeles' two best players. He hit 29.7 percent of his threes in 130 games with the Lakers, who posted a better net rating when Westbrook was off the floor.

The Lakers would have been better off just keeping Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Kyle Kuzma but instead onboarded Westbrook, who was still owed $93.1 million over the final two years of his deal. To get rid of Russ in 2023, the Lakers had to take on Jarred Vanderbilt's bad salary and surrender a 2027 first-round pick.

4. Kings Swap Tyrese Haliburton for Domantas Sabonis in 2022

The Trade: Sacramento Kings acquire Domantas Sabonis, Justin Holiday, Jeremy Lamb and a 2023 second-round pick from the Indiana Pacers for Tyrese Haliburton, Buddy Hield and Tristan Thompson

This deal was dubious for Sacramento at the time, as Haliburton had already shown flashes of the ability that would make him an All-NBA force and leader of a Pacers team that was a single win from a championship in 2025. Now, four years removed from it, the trade only looks worse for the Kings.

Back then, you could talk yourself into Sabonis as an upgrade. Haliburton had already dealt with some injury concerns and hadn't really proved anything yet, while Sabonis brought size and a cleaner theoretical fit next to De'Aaron Fox. The Kings even made the playoffs in 2023, the first time that'd happened since 2006.

That success proved to be short-lived. Fox is long gone, Sabonis isn't currently tradable for positive value and the Kings are right back in the "this is embarrassing" tier of the NBA's hierarchy.

Meanwhile, Haliburton is indisputably one of the league's best offensive players and team leaders—a transformative force with the rare ability to make all of his teammates better with his cleverness, efficiency and unselfish attitude.

The only solace for the Kings is that Haliburton probably couldn't have become what he did with the Pacers if he'd stayed in Sacramento. Even that has to sting. Any franchise mismanaged badly enough to stifle talent like his should be asking itself some serious questions.

The Trade: Phoenix Suns acquire Kevin Durant and TJ Warren from the Brooklyn Nets for Mikal Bridges, Cam Johnson, Jae Crowder, 2023 first-round pick, 2025 first-round pick, 2027 first-round pick, 2029 first-round pick, 2028 first-round swap

Kevin Durant made his first trade request in June of 2022, naming the Suns as his preferred destination. No deal came to pass, so KD made a second request at the 2023 deadline. Somehow, with the whole world knowing he was unhappy and dead set on landing in Phoenix, the Nets still extracted an absolute haul.

Usually, when a player narrows his choices to one team, the lack of a bidding war keeps the return lower. Not so here, and the Suns will be feeling the pain of shipping out five first-round assets for the rest of the decade.

The price was too high under any circumstances, but this trade looks doubly bad because Phoenix was a mere six games over .500 across Durant's two full seasons. When KD predictably hurt the vibes with his fourth team and had to be shipped to his fifth (the Houston Rockets), the Suns only managed to get back a single first-round asset in the exchange.

2. Phoenix Suns Acquire Bradley Beal in 2023

The Trade: Phoenix Suns acquire Bradley Beal from the Washington Wizards for Chris Paul, Landry Shamet, No. 7 (Bilal Coulibaly), 2024 first-round swap, 2026 first-round swap, 2028 first-round swap, 2030 first-round swap, 2024 second-round pick, 2025 second-round pick, 2026 second-round pick, 2027 second-round pick, 2028 second-round pick, 2030 second-round pick

Well, if you thought the Suns had blown through all of their assets in the KD deal, you were wrong. New owner Mat Ishbia was intent on building what he believed to be a powerhouse and was willing to completely nuke every last asset in his misguided pursuit of short-term success.

Phoenix ceded control of every first-round asset it retained after the Durant deal, sending first-round swap rights on four first-rounders plus a heap of seconds to land Beal.

The Beal acquisition rates worse than the Durant one because the former wasn't healthy or productive with the Suns and ultimately had to be waived and stretched. Phoenix got zero assets for cutting Beal loose and will pay him $19.4 million every year through 2029-30.

1. Mavericks Trade Away Luka Dončić in 2025

The Trade: Dallas Mavericks acquire Anthony Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick from the Los Angeles Lakers for Luka Dončić, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris

The first rule of having Luka Dončić on your team is that you should not trade Luka Dončić unless Luka Dončić specifically asks you to trade him.

The second rule is that if you have Luka Dončić on your team and Luka Dončić specifically asks you to trade him, you shop around so you get the best possible deal.

Led by the since-fired Nico Harrison, the Dallas Mavericks broke both of those rules and will have to wear the distinction of making the worst trade in recent memory until some other sad-sack franchise ships outs its cornerstone for a pittance.

Whether Dallas tried to frame it as a long- or short-term move, the logic was flawed. Dončić was the better and more durable player at the time, and he was six years younger than AD.

Just imagine how much worse this deal would look if the Mavs hadn't lucked into the top spot in the 2025 lottery, which landed them Cooper Flagg, a human memory-wipe who gave fans something new to focus on.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.standfirst: Los graves problemas económicos del AS Mónaco le excluyen del baloncesto profesional francés
articles.summary: Los graves problemas económicos del AS Mónaco le excluyen del baloncesto profesional francés
articles.body: Han pasado 15 meses desde que el AS Mónaco acariciara la gloria alcanzando la final de la Euroliga, donde perdió ante el Fenerbahce. Ahora, después de una imparable caída a los infiernos, ha sido excluido definitivamente del baloncesto profesional pese a que la temporada pasada ganó todos los títulos en que había en juego en Francia. La Federación Francesa se ha negado a reabrir el caso del conjunto del Principado, acuciado por los problemas económicos. El club aún podría acudir al Tribunal Administrativo, pero algunas fuentes indican que no lo hará. Así que, sin posibilidad de participar en la Betclic ÉLITE ni en la ÉLITE 2, en el mejor de los escenarios lo haría en la Nationale 1, tercera categoría del baloncesto galo, algo que ya le sucedió en 2004 al histórico Limoges, campeón de Europa en 1993. La dramática situación del AS Mónaco viene provocada por los problemas financieros de su propietario, el multimillonario ruso-húngaro Alexei Fedorychev, cuyas cuentas fueron embargadas por la guerra de Ucrania. Sin su capital, comenzaron las penurias que sufrió el equipo la temporada pasada: impagos, sanciones sin poder fichar, marcha de jugadores y del entrenador Vassilis Spanoulis, amenazas de huelga antes de partidos de Liga... Fue un milagro que, con ese panorama y en ocasiones con una plantilla llena de jugadores júniors, conquistaran los cuatro títulos del baloncesto francés. Ayudó una inyección económica de 30 millones de euros procedente del Principado a través de la Compañía Nacional de Financiación, pero los estamentos del deporte galo han considerado ahora que no había garantías suficientes para poder inscribir al equipo en las competiciones profesionales. La aparición como posible salvador de Jamal Mashburn, exjugador de la NBA, ha sido un sainete. Este verano, después de todo lo vivido, el AS Mónaco vio partir a las estrellas que aún permanecías en la plantilla: Elie Okobo y Jaron Blossomgame se fueron a Dubái, Alpha Diallo jugará en los Nuggets, Mike James y Matthew Strazel estarán a las órdenes de Pablo Laso en el Anadolu Efes y Daniel Theis se ha comprometido con el Maccabi Tel Aviv tras haber firmado previamente con el ASVEL Villeurbanne, otro equipo francés cuyas elevadas pretensiones se han visto recortadas por cuestiones económicas.

articles.title: “Refused to do for so long”: WNBA Analyst Accuses League of Pushing Caitlin Clark Away as FIBA Takes Over
articles.summary: The impact and drawing power of Caitlin Clark in women’s basketball and the broader women’s sports landscape is mathematically and culturally undeniable. And...
articles.body:
The impact and drawing power of Caitlin Clark in women's basketball and the broader women's sports landscape is mathematically and culturally undeniable. And unlike the WNBA, which through repeated actions appears to deliberately minimise that reality, FIBA Women's Basketball is leaning directly into it.

According to the WNBA analyst who hosts the Keep the Vision channel on YouTube, FIBA appears to be placing Caitlin Clark at the centre of its promotional push for the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, which kicks off on September 4. And in his view, this is precisely the approach the WNBA needs to adopt, capitalising on the extraordinary commercial and cultural gravity Clark brings to the game.

"FIBA, they understand the Caitlin Clark effect, the Caitlin Clark greatness worldwide," the KTV host said in a reaction video shared on Saturday . "FIBA has already done something that the WNBA has dragged its feet on and refused to do for so long. They have gone all in on Caitlin Clark being the face not only of the United States basketball team, but of the entire FIBA World Cup. FIBA is leaning in on Caitlin Clark, leading the way for this FIBA World Cup competition.

"WNBA, take notes. Why is it that people internationally can understand and respect the greatness and all the attention that Caitlin Clark brings to the game, but the people here can't do it? Why is it that the PGA Tour and the NBA and Major League Baseball and the NFL — all these other big-time leagues — can respect and appreciate the greatness of Caitlin Clark and welcome her with open arms, except the WNBA?"

The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup begins in Berlin, Germany, in approximately five days. And despite this being Clark's debut at the tournament, FIBA appears to already fully recognise the phenomenon she represents. As the KTV host pointed out, a number of posts on their official X page have spotlighted her upcoming debut. As seen on their X page, a ranking of the top 20 players to watch in the tournament also placed Clark seventh overall. That makes her the highest-ranked newcomer on the entire list. FIBA even got a post highlighting her MVP-winning performance at the qualifying tournament in March.

And with a FIBA website publication that the WNBA analyst pointed out, it does seem like Caitlin Clark is the player fans are most excited to see in this competition. And by a mile. The publication features a poll asking fans which player they are most excited to watch from the top 20 players FIBA highlighted.

An August 26 Athlon Sports report said Clark led FIBA's online fan poll with 48% of votes at the time of publication, with A'ja Wilson second at 17%.

That overwhelming fan enthusiasm mirrors what has been unmistakably visible in the WNBA since Clark entered the league. She has consistently driven historic viewership and fundamentally altered the financial and commercial metrics of women's professional basketball.

One of the most recent and striking examples came on Sunday, when the Chicago Sky-Indiana Fever game averaged 3.31 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, making it the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since the league's opening weekend in 1997.

And if there is any doubt about the driving force behind those numbers, every single one of the top five most-watched WNBA games of the 2026 season has featured Caitlin Clark. In fact, she has broken network-specific viewership records for CBS, NBC, ESPN, and ION throughout the year.

Yet despite all of that, the WNBA seems to continue falling short of the standard FIBA appears to be setting in terms of simply recognising and celebrating what Clark represents. Their 30th Anniversary poster earlier this season did not include her. A recent NCAA post highlighting record-breaking former collegiate stars in the WNBA also left her out.

Some of these omissions might be explained away by rights issues or editorial choices. But when the pattern repeats itself this frequently, it becomes very difficult to dismiss as coincidence.

articles.title: "I'm Beating Bronny (James)": Popular YouTuber IShowSpeed Makes Bold Claim on Lakers Star
articles.summary: “I’m Beating Bronny (James)”: Popular YouTuber IShowSpeed Makes Bold Claim on Lakers StarBronny James has already shown that he can move on a basketball cour...
articles.body:
Bronny James has already shown that he can move on a basketball court. Now, a clip of the Lakers guard doing something completely different has IShowSpeed convinced that he has found a matchup he can win.

Speed came across footage of James playing soccer and could not believe what he was seeing.

"Wait, why does Bronny look kinda nice?" Speed said while reacting to the clip, which was shared by Bleacher Report on Instagram Saturday.

"Bro, in football, bro, I am beating Bronny in football. Y'all know me, I'm literally one of the best footballers alive."

To be fair, Speed has done enough on a soccer field to make the claim more than just talk.

He has played in several charity soccer games and scored for the YouTube All Stars in their victory at the 2025 Sidemen Charity Match at Wembley Stadium. He also scored twice in the 2026 YouTube FIFA Creator Cup in Central Park.

But Bronny has some history with the sport too.

Long before basketball became his main focus, James played soccer growing up. He even helped his sixth-grade team win a soccer league championship.

James also revealed that background while speaking to reporters ahead of the 2024 NBA Draft.

"Nah. I mean, I played other sports," James said. "I played soccer. Wasn't allowed to play football by mom, didn't allow that."

The "football" James mentioned there was American football. His father, LeBron James, played the sport as a wide receiver at St. Vincent-St. Mary, but Bronny's mother did not allow him to play it.

And James' old skills were still pretty easy to spot when he stepped onto the field again in August 2026. During an informal game, his ball control and footwork stood out to spectators, particularly because fans are much more used to seeing him with a basketball in his hands. He had shown off similar footwork at Fanatics Fan Fest earlier in the year.

That is where Speed's challenge gets a little more interesting.

Soccer has been a huge part of Speed's rise online. His obsession with the sport became especially well known after a livestream donation asking him to name his favorite player led to his now-famous Cristiano Ronaldo reaction.

Since then, Speed has met Ronaldo, followed the sport around the world and even performed at a closing ceremony connected to the 2026 World Cup.

So Speed certainly has the soccer résumé and the confidence to make this interesting.

Bronny, however, has a much bigger basketball season waiting for him.

The 2026-27 season will be his third with the Lakers, who are moving into a new era after LeBron left Los Angeles for the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency. The Lakers have also decided to protect Bronny's $2.3 million salary for next season, and he is already preparing for the new campaign alongside Luka Dončić in Slovenia.

A Bronny-Speeed soccer showdown probably is not happening anytime soon.

But after seeing what James can do with the ball at his feet, Speed has already decided how it would end.

articles.title: Phoenix Mercury sees younger players develop ahead of World Cup break
articles.summary: The Phoenix Mercury saw younger players take the court in the final game before the FIBA World Cup break on Aug. 29.
articles.body:
The dog days of the season are nearly over for the Phoenix Mercury, but not without some complications caused by the upcoming FIBA World Cup break that will make it a 17-day wait for the remaining four games of the WNBA season.

Phoenix (14-26) has already been eliminated from the playoffs, but saw a promising showing from its younger players in the 101-69 win against the Toronto Tempo on Saturday, Aug. 29.

"It's been a frustrating and challenging year for everyone, but this definitely felt great, especially going on the break," coach Nate Tibbetts said.

The Mercury were shorthanded with four players out ahead of the World Cup, including guard Kahleah Copper, guard Kelsey Plum, forward Valeriane Ayayi and center Kyara Linskens.

All four players will represent their respective countries, with Ayayi representing France, Linskens representing Belgium and Plum and Copper representing the U.S.

Phoenix Mercury host Toronto Tempo ahead of FIBA World Cup break

Copper was a game-time decision with a left ankle issue and warmed up, but didn't play. Tibbetts said he hopes the two will be healthy enough to play in the World Cup. Team USA's first game of the World Cup starts at 5:15 a.m. MT on Sept. 4.

The Mercury's rotation had already shifted earlier in the week when forward DeWanna Bonner took a contract buyout on Aug. 24, moving Natasha Mack back to the starting center.

In turn, Mack, Alyssa Thomas and Noemie Brochant were the only veterans remaining in the frontcourt.

At the start of the game, it was veterans like guard Sami Whitcomb running the offense with eight points and 2-for-3 shooting from 3-point range. She finished with a season-high of 14 points and shot 4-for-6 from 3-point range.

But the younger players provided some energy against an injury-depleted Toronto team. Forward Maddy Westbeld showed more awareness in her third game with the Mercury, drawing contact when she couldn't find any open passes and getting to the free-throw line.

Guard Kara Dunn found confidence from the perimeter in her WNBA debut, draining three 3-pointers on three looks in her first seven minutes.

Dunn participated in training camp with the Mercury, but dealt with a lingering knee issue and didn't make the opening-night roster. She returned on a developmental contract on July 26.

"For me, it means a lot because me and Sami share similar journeys this year," Dunn said. "Getting comfortable is important to me and showcasing everything that I can do is just one step, but I was really happy with what I've seen so far."

Guard Shay Ciezki had a better feel for her two-way playmaking in her fourth game, matching Brochant for the team lead in scoring with 15 points, along with five assists.

Tibbetts and his coaching staff have seen the younger players stay in the gym the longest during practice and play for limited minutes.

"It's hard when you're not playing," Tibbetts said. "You got to love it to continue to want to get better. We've got some young players that are doing that, and that's the reason our staff is pouring into them for opportunities like this. It's good to get reps and feel on film instead of in practice."

The Mercury's youth movement resulted in the team hitting a season high of 153-pointers . The Mercury alsoscored 49 bench points and 28 fast-break points.

Phoenix played only the reserves in the fourth quarter and went scoreless for nearly five minutes, but eventually reached the 100-point mark for the fifth time this season.

Tibbetts and Hannah Wengertsman, the team's trainer, will head to Berlin as part of Team USA's staff for the World Cup.

The Mercury players not heading to Germany will take a full week off, then return for four to five days of individual workouts with the remaining staff, as they await the return of Tibbetts, Copper, Plum, Ayayi and Linskens.

Once the rest of the team returns, there will be two or three practices before the team heads to Portland on Sept. 17.

"It's nice to get a little bit of time to go home and be with family, to do whatever you want to do and reset," Whitcomb said. "And obviously, we'll come back and still have time to get on court and keep working and keep building and doing all of the things we want to do. We take these last four games seriously, and we want to maximize those reps on court together and what we're trying to build for next year."

The WNBA unveiled a new Finals logo with the playoffs looming on the horizon.

For the first time since 2006 , the league is showcasing the championship trophy in the primary design.

The regular season is set to wrap up on Sept. 24 following a pause due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.

The eight playoff teams are already confirmed, though there's plenty of movement in the seedings to come. The Minnesota Lynx sit in the top spot and have a three-game lead on the Golden State Valkyries.

articles.title: Bebe Rexha Addresses Dating Rumors with Knicks Champion Jordan Clarkson After Viral Photo
articles.summary: After a viral photo surfaced late last month featuring New York Knicks veteran guard Jordan Clarkson and pop star Bebe Rexha, many wondered if a romance was brewing between the two celebrities.
articles.body:
After a viral photo surfaced late last month featuring New York Knicks veteran guard Jordan Clarkson and pop star Bebe Rexha, many wondered if a romance was brewing between the two celebrities.

However, TMZ recently asked Rexha if there were any "sparks" between her and Clarkson, and she "quickly shut it down, shaking her head no," adding that she and the newly crowned NBA champion are just "friends."

Clarkson and Rexha were seen together at a Vogue fashion event at Rockefeller Center in New York City near the end of July. Prior to the event, they spent the whole day together in the city, including hosting an art session alongside artist Leopoldo Gout.

Rexha celebrated her 37th birthday this weekend, and there weren't any indications that Clarkson was in attendance.

Without a romance on the horizon, Clarkson can focus on preparing for the upcoming NBA season as the Knicks try to defend their title.

articles.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson Declared 'The King' by NYC Mayor Mamdani in Trending Video
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is well aware of the hierarchy in the Big Apple following the New York Knicks' 2026 NBA championship win.
articles.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is well aware of the hierarchy in the Big Apple following the New York Knicks' 2026 NBA championship win.

Mamdani had a fun interaction with a child over the weekend while they were roasting marshmallows, and it ended with him giving a well-deserved title to Knicks star point guard Jalen Brunson.

"You could become the king," the child suggested.

"I'm happy as the mayor," Mamdani responded before leaning over and whispering, "Jalen Brunson is the king."

Brunson endeared himself to NYC since joining the Knicks in 2022, and he solidified his spot as one of the greatest sports figures in New York history by leading the franchise to its first NBA title since 1973.

It's safe to say that Mamdani isn't the only New Yorker to have officially crowned Brunson as King of NYC.

articles.title: George Klassen placed on injured list
articles.summary: The Angels place young arm on the injured list for lower back tightness, but they hope it's a short stint.
articles.body:
ANAHEIM — The Angels' starting rotation took a blow before Sunday afternoon's game against the Phillies with the announcement that right-hander George Klassen was heading to the 15-day injured list with lower back inflammation.

Klassen said he began feeling more sore than usual the morning after making his start on Monday night. Despite the trip to the injured list with only a month to go in the season, Klassen isn't concerned about this being an issue for long.

"Some movements feel a little restricted, but I mean, we're making progress right now," Klassen said.

He's still playing catch and said that his back does feel better than it did on Tuesday, but he and the Angels don't want to rush anything.

"Just out of precaution," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said of putting Klassen on the injured list. "You want to make sure that we can get it before it turns into something big. But he's not concerned about it. We're not concerned about it. But just to stay ahead of it."

Suzuki also said they have not talked about managing Klassen's innings yet. His 118 innings pitched between Triple-A Salt Lake and the majors is the most of his professional career.

Things were trending up for the 24-year-old before landing on the injured list.

Since being called back up at the beginning of August, he's pitched to a 2.01 ERA in four starts with 18 strikeouts in 22 1/3 innings.

"He's been making huge strides," Suzuki said. "I think the consistency and those types of things have been getting better and better every time it gets out. And you can kind of see the comfort level, I think, within every start. It gets a little bit more comfortable for every start and seeing the results."

As tough as a blow this is to the rotation, it does temporarily solve a problem the Angels have.

The Angels have been operating with a six-man rotation since left-hander Yusei Kikuchi came off the injured list last week. This has shortened the bullpen, which has paid the price.

Since going to the six-man rotation, the Angels' bullpen has a 5.18 ERA in 24 1/3 innings of work. That's put a damper on the hot streak the bullpen had previously been on, ranking as the 5th-best bullpen since the All-Star break with a 3.12 ERA in 121 1/3 innings.

Klassen was slated to start on Monday, so that will push everyone up a day in the rotation. Right-hander Walbert Ureña will start in the series opener against the Yankees on Monday.

The Angels also announced they optioned right-hander Trevor Martin to Triple-A Salt Lake and they recalled left-handers Mitch Farris and Blake Weiman.

articles.title: Academy to host Katy youth basketball tournament with Nike, Jordan. Here's how to sign up.
articles.summary: Six half-courts will run simultaneously in front of the Katy store.
articles.body:
An Academy Sports and Outdoors store in Katy plans to host a three-on-three youth basketball tournament for up to 128 teams from across the region in October.

Academy partnered with Nike and the Jordan Brand to organize the event, which will take place in front of the store at 23155 Katy Freeway on Oct. 17 and 18, according to the local sporting goods company. Six half-courts in the store's front lot will run simultaneous games for boys and girls in middle and high school, and the double-elimination tournament will last through much of Saturday and Sunday.

The event, dubbed the H-Town Classic, will raise money for the Boys and Girls Clubs of Greater Houston to support youth programs and community development , according to Academy.

"Houston's basketball tradition runs deep, and we're proud to partner with Nike and Jordan Brand to continue the legacy with the H-Town Classic," Academy CEO Steve Lawrence said in a release. "This tournament captures the excitement and community spirit that make basketball such an important part of our city while creating opportunities for athletes of all skill levels to participate, compete and have fun."

The H-Town Classic is set to stretch from 8:30 a.m, to 7 p,m. on Saturday and Sunday. Teams from across the Houston area will descend onto the Katy lot, and each will play at least two games, according to Academy.

Two noteworthy locals are slated to emcee: Kiotti Brown, the voice of the Rockets, and Tausha Sanders, the founder of Her Grails, an organization for female sneaker fans. Other activities, food trucks and giveaways are also set to surround the action on the court.

To register a team, you must complete this form on Academy's website . A team can compete in one of four divisions - middle school boys, middle school girls, high school boys and high school girls.

Each entry costs $100, and registration will be open either through Oct. 9 or until each division reaches capacity, according to Academy. Each division will have a 32-team bracket, totaling 128 teams across the entire tournament, its website states.

Teams can register up to four players, but only three at a time can play, according to the website. Every player will receive a team jersey through the event, according to Academy.

Boys and Girls Club of Houston participants will also get two free team entries, store officials said.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Thanks Celtics After 76ers Trade, Fans Hold NBA Trophy in Viral Videos of Block Party
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown thanked Boston Celtics fans during his appearance at the "741 Frequency Fest: A Love Letter to Boston Block Party" on Sunday at Boston Commons.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown thanked Boston Celtics fans during his appearance at the "741 Frequency Fest: A Love Letter to Boston Block Party" on Sunday at Boston Commons.

Brown was shockingly traded to the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason for Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks.

Brown, 29, spent his first 10 NBA seasons in Boston and they were memorable. He was a one-time champion, five-time All-Star and two-time All-NBA selection during his time with the organization, averaging 20 points, 5.5 rebounds and 2.9 assists per contest.

With Jayson Tatum missing most of the 2025-26 season, Brown stepped up in a major way, putting up 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists. But the Celtics chose to not only trade him, but also to an Eastern Conference rival.

Still, Brown's time in Boston was important to him, as he reflected on Sunday.

"When I got to this city I said I'm gonna go to war for this city," he said at the event. "I met so many great people here. People that helped me in the community, that motivated me on my journey. People that have supported me even when I didn't support myself at times. I just want to say thank you to Boston. Thank you to the city, and I love you."

Boston's decision to trade Brown to the Sixers, however, had quite the domino effect. LeBron James chose to sign with the team in the offseason shortly thereafter, giving Philly arguably the scariest starting lineup in the sport, with that duo pairing with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

Expectations are high in Philadelphia. But Brown's fondness for the city of Boston clearly remains intact.
